body.x: AETECH (CEO Taehyung Park) announced at CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and tech exhibition held in Las Vegas early last month, that it has enhanced its potential for global market entry through AI- and robot-based waste-sorting technology.

AETECH is a deep-tech startup that showcases AI-driven, automated waste-sorting solutions using vision and robotics. The company explains that its technology addresses structural issues in waste treatment, such as high labor intensity, low sorting efficiency, and quality variability, thereby improving resource recovery rates and supporting sustainable operations.

Previously, AETECH introduced the sorting robot Aitron, which classifies up to 96 pieces of waste per minute with 99.3% accuracy, and accumulated rich empirical and commercialization results by supplying about 30 robots to 11 public and private waste sorting plants in Korea by the end of last year.

Subsequently, by accelerating its globalization strategy through discussions focused on the Asia and Oceania regions, the company increased its external recognition by winning a CES 2026 Innovation Award for multi-tron, designed for installation and operation in urban and multi-purpose spaces.

The multi-tron, which won the award, is a modular resource circulation station solution. It features a compact design where the AI system automatically recognizes and sorts waste as soon as a user inputs it. Accordingly, it can implement resource-recovery functions across various urban spaces, particularly in multi-use facilities such as public housing, shopping malls, and stadiums.

While presenting this urban resource circulation model that boasts superior accessibility and scalability compared to existing large-scale sorting plant-centered infrastructure, AETECH also introduced airo-mrf, an automated resource circulation facility built by integrating its technologies, earning favorable reviews from industry officials.

body.x: AETECH successfully laid the foundation for expanding sales channels by attracting 47 export consultations at CES 2026, leveraging its innovative technology, and recorded a cumulative consultation value of USD 28.8 million (approximately 42.036 billion KRW).

An AETECH official said, “Through this CES, we promoted AETECH’s technology that maximizes the efficiency of waste management to the world and confirmed intense interest from buyers of various nationalities.” They added, “We feel pleased to gain momentum for entering the North American and European markets in line with the global carbon-neutral trend.”

They continued, “Based on the in-depth discussions shared during the exhibition, we will pursue the advancement and customization of our technology and solidify our position as a representative Korean AI environmental tech company contributing to solving global environmental problems.” They emphasized, “Furthermore, we will grow into a company that leads the global market and standards with waste sorting technology.”

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
